title: Create contract negotiation fast-track & redline escalation playbook for MSA/DPA terms
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Problem: We continue to incur long cycle-times and ad-hoc concessions when negotiating MSAs and DPAs at scale. Redlines that touch liability caps, indemnity scope, or data residency trigger full legal review and slow down sales. There is no single source-of-truth for pre-approved concessions by deal size or customer tier.

Goal: Ship a documented fast-track negotiation playbook and escalation workflow that reduces time-to-signature for standard enterprise deals while preserving legal guardrails for high-risk clauses. The playbook will: intake redlines, auto-classify risk tier, provide canned responses and fallback concessions, define signature authority thresholds, and standardize routing to counsel for exceptional cases.

Scope: MSA and DPA redlines from customers and channel partners. Excludes bespoke SOW negotiation and third-party reseller agreements. Integrates with Salesforce & Zendesk intake channels and with Legal (in-house counsel) triage queue.

Out-of-scope: Complete contract overhaul, new billing/legal templates (separate project), and on-prem licensing terms (handled by Private team).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Single playbook doc in Confluence with step-by-step intake and triage flow.
2) Auto-classifier prototype (rules + sample keyword heuristics) that maps redlines into risk tiers: low/medium/high.
3) A set of pre-approved concession strings for common asks (liability cap variations, indemnity carve-outs, warranty periods) approved by legal.
4) Routing matrix implemented: when to route to Legal, Sales Ops, or Finance.
5) Measurable SLA targets published (e.g., <3 business days for low-risk, <7 business days for medium, immediate escalation for high).
6) Pilot with three sales deals and documented outcomes (time-to-sign, concessions accepted).
success_metrics:
- Median time-to-execution for pilot deals reduced by >=40%.
- % of redlines resolved without full legal review >= 60% after pilot.
- Concessions cost (estimated liability exposure) within pre-approved thresholds for >=90% of accepted concessions.
- Positive sales feedback (>=4/5) on usability of playbook and templates.
risks_and_tradeoffs:
- Overly permissive pre-approved concessions could increase legal/financial exposure.
- Overly strict playbook will push deals to Enterprise sales motions and increase cycle time.
- Automating classification risks mis-categorization; initial phase must be conservative.
- Resource trade-off: legal time for playbook creation vs. faster deal closures.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0 (2 weeks): intake form + manual triage + build canonical concession list.
Phase 1 (3 weeks): implement automated classifier heuristics and canned response templates; legal review of pre-approved concessions.
Phase 2 (2 weeks): pilot with 3-5 active deals across SMB, mid-market, and enterprise; collect metrics.
Phase 3 (ongoing): refine classifier, expand templates, and integrate routing into Salesforce.

Stakeholders: Product (owner), Sales Ops, Legal, Finance, Customer Success, Security.
open_questions:
- What are signature authority thresholds by revenue band? (Finance input required)
- Do we allow limited data-processor subprocessor exceptions in the DPA fast-track?
- Should certain security questionnaire results (e.g., failing a critical control) automatically trigger high-risk routing?
- Level of documentation required for exceptions (audit trail for concessions)?
next_steps:
- Align with Legal on root list of acceptable concessions (due 2026-03-20).
- Build a lightweight intake form for redlines and link it to a shared triage inbox (owner: Sales Ops).
- Prototype simple keyword-based classifier rules and run on 50 historical redlines to measure false positive rate.
- Schedule a 45-minute sync with Finance to pick liability/insurance thresholds.
- Prepare pilot candidate list with AE owners.
